parsed_answer.content: EnumSet is a specialized, highly optimized Set implementation designed specifically for use with enum types in Java. Under the hood, EnumSet leverages a bit vector implementation, meaning every single element in the set is represented by a single bit within a primitive word (typically a 64-bit long) or an array of primitive words if the enum contains more than 64 constants. This architecture completely eliminates the memory overhead and hashing cost associated with standard collection classes like HashSet or TreeSet. Because enum constants are known completely at compile time and have a fixed, finite set of values, the Java compiler and runtime can map them directly to ordinal integer positions. Operations such as add, remove, and contains execute in constant time $O(1)$, translating directly down to ultra-fast bitwise arithmetic operations like bitwise OR, AND, and NOT. When working with flags, status codes, or mutually exclusive state configurations in high-performance Java applications, EnumSet stands out as the ultimate choice for both memory efficiency and CPU cache locality.

items: RegularEnumSet is utilized when the enum has 64 or fewer constants, packing all elements into a single primitive long field inside the set instance, ensuring zero heap allocation overhead during iteration or modification.

JumboEnumSet is automatically instantiated via factory methods when the target enum exceeds 64 constants, utilizing a long array to hold the bit vector representation while maintaining the exact same high-performance bitwise execution semantics.

Iterators returned by EnumSet do not traverse pointers or linked node structures; instead, they compute the indices of set bits sequentially using Long.numberOfTrailingZeros, resulting in exceptional CPU cache efficiency.

parsed_answer.content: Never instantiate an EnumSet using the new keyword; the constructors are intentionally package-private. Always use factory methods like EnumSet.allOf(), EnumSet.noneOf(), or EnumSet.of() to let the internal factory dynamically select between RegularEnumSet and JumboEnumSet based on the enum's size.
